title: SuperSawBrs — estimated opening excerpt
method: Source-only analysis: mono 22050 Hz decoding of the original Roland MP3, 8192-sample Hann STFT at 256-sample hops, nonnegative least-squares decomposition against detune-broadened harmonic templates over MIDI 36–88, and inspection of local FFT peaks and amplitude transitions. Candidate notes were screened for upper-harmonic and subharmonic errors. The first phrase is centred on sounding F2/F3/F4 with a moving middle voice C4, Bb3 and Ab3; the second phrase moves the bass to Ab2 at roughly 4.05 seconds. FFT peaks at about 86/176/261/353 Hz support the opening voicing. Repeated amplitude attacks provide the brass-stab rhythm; intermediate beat-induced peaks were excluded. Inspection of the first rendered comparison exposed a source bass family that continues through upper-voice gaps; F2 and Ab2 are therefore encoded as held bass notes rather than repeated stabs.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI is unavailable. Every event here is estimated from the MP3, not an exact original MIDI event.
Velocity 100 is an explicit placeholder. Original velocities, sustain pedal, pitch bend, modulation and other controller events are unavailable and are not recovered.

Sounding pitch families do not uniquely determine played keys when oscillator octave offsets or layered tones are unknown. This transcription uses sounding fundamentals with a newly designed patch at zero overall transpose.
MP3 encoding, detuned oscillators, effects and envelope release obscure key-down and key-up times. The MIDI contains practical gates, not measured hardware key releases.
The patch is newly authored in Septum from spectral and temporal cues. It is an approximation of the named factory sound, not Roland factory SysEx or a recovered hardware preset.
Octave doubling at F3/F4 may partly be oscillator harmonics rather than separately pressed keys. It is an explicit voicing assumption in this approximation.

The bass is estimated as held through upper-voice gaps. Whether F3/F4 were also held, or retriggered with the middle voice, remains unknown; the upper voicing is retriggered to reproduce broad attacks.
Brass attack and effect tails leave gate estimates uncertain by roughly 30–100 ms. The 8-second crop truncates the transition into the following phrase.

patch_design.name: APX SawBrs
rationale: Dense spread harmonic peaks motivate two moderately detuned Super Saw oscillators.
The rounded onset followed by a darker held body suggests a short positive filter attack and a medium filter decay; amplitude gates retain the pronounced stabs.

Comparison of the first render showed overly bright chord stabs and overly deep gaps. The cutoff/envelope were softened and release lengthened; sustained bass is now represented separately in the estimated MIDI.
uncertainties: No authenticated factory PRESET dump is available; every changed control value is an authored approximation.
The recording does not uniquely reveal oscillator topology, layer routing, filter slope, modulation or effect settings.
The octave chord voicing and single-tone topology are approximations; exact hardware layer allocation is unknown.
A first software render informed these control adjustments. This is a conditional audio match using estimated notes, not recovered factory settings or a hardware-calibrated DSP claim.
